text.p: Nabisco Holdings Corp. Thursday said third-quarter profits rose 35 percent and that it expected strong results for the rest of the year.

The maker of cookies, crackers and snack said net income rose to $70 million, or 26 cents a share, in the quarter, from $52 million, or 20 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter. The latest results were reduced by one-time expenses related to a restructuring, and the year-ago figure was also reduced by an extraordinary item.
Sales grew 10 percent to $2.24 billion from $2.04 billion.
The Parsippany, N.J.-based company said that excluding the impact of the restructuring costs, operating income for the quarter rose 15 percent to $225 million from $196 million in 1995.

Domestic sales grew 7 percent to $1.58 billion from $1.47 billion, fuelled by sales of Oreo and Chips Ahoy! cookies and Ritz crackers, as well the new Air Crisp line, the company said. But sales of SnackWell's and Newtons fell as did breakfast snacks such as Pop Tarts.
International sales rose 16 percent to $660 million from $570 million, though profit margins fell because of higher commodity costs.
"We're satisfied with our third-quarter operating results," Chairman H. John Greeniaus said in a statement accompanying the results.
Nabisco said sales in its core products and cost savings stemming from this year's restructuring of domestic and international businesses should help fourth-quarter results.

"Looking ahead, we see the momentum in our business continuing to strengthen," Greeniaus said. "Our focus on highly profitable, core products, coupled with the anticipated cost savings from our restructuring, put us in an excellent position for a strong fourth quarter."
Nabisco's stock fell 62.5 cents to $34.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
